title: Does anyone have experience building complex first person animations?
author: Stefan474
selftext:
Hey all, 

Small background - I am a senior SWE, have some gamedev experience in personal projects and decided to try and make a game with all the cool showcases I've seen with opus/sonnet creating some gorgeous stuff. 

The game is a first person swordfighting game, where hand animations are kind of important, like hand resting on a sheathed katana, blocking by lifting it and holding with two hands, using the free hand for other abilities, kicking etc. 

The problem is that no matter what workflow I try, the hands look beyond garbage. 

I tried to use opus 5.5 as a taste judge for a review loop, tried giving it tools like the blender mcp, tried giving it infinite tokens to review and improve until it looks good and natural, tried giving it references, tried with different models in their own worktrees, tried having it find assets and adapting them, and every time hands/arms look like sludge and the poses for the sword are awkward and unnatural. 

Does anyone have a good tool stack I can try to use to one shot/iterate on this or a way to get AI to set me up with a workflow where I can tweak it in 3d. 

Besides that though the shaders and scenes it made are gorgeous, and it adheres very well to my prompts for making and tweaking game mechanics.

Using godot and blender with antrhopic models.

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: Cheaper to just buy your animations on actorcore. But if that's not an option, you can use video to 3d motion capture and do the animations yourself and ask opus to keyframe the animation you just gave it
